blind_target.authors: Salmela, V. R., & Laurinen, P. I.
blind_target.title: Low-level features determine brightness in White’s and Benary’s illusions.
blind_target.evidence_quote:
We replicated and extended Salmela and Laurinen’s (2009) results, and
     tested a number of diferent multi-scale spatial iltering models with respect to
     their capability to reproduce the psychophysically observed efects of narrow-
     band noise on lightness perception.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
Still, despite these diiculties with interpreting precisely what the
     lightness matches mean, the data consistently demonstrate that for most ob-
     servers, noise in the range from 1 to 5 cpd has the largest efect on perceived
     lightness, and that the most efective noise frequency does not scale propor-
     tionally to the grating frequency.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The stated original noise-masking finding is observed again: strongest masking from 1 to 5 cpd. Tests of theoretical models with new stimuli are not reanalyses of original data.

luna_triage.reason: The source explicitly says it replicated Salmela and Laurinen (2009), whose reported empirical finding is that narrowband noise from 1 to 5 cpd strongly masked brightness illusions. The supplied White (1979) row is the illusion stimulus source, not the noise-masking finding.
